docs.title: Baton-C — deterministic messaging over one UART wire
docs.text: Quick start

docs.title: A minimal slave in one file
docs.text:
The application owns one struct baton_node, gives it a write function for the UART and a callback for received messages, passes every received byte from the UART interrupt and calls baton_node_process() every millisecond. This slave publishes its uptime as a state and acknowledges every CMD_SET_OUTPUT event with an OUTPUT_REPORT event.

#include "baton.h"

static const uint8_t slaves[] = {0x11U, 0x12U};
static struct baton_node node;

static int uart_write(void* context, const uint8_t* data, size_t length)
{
    (void) context;
    return board_uart_write(data, length); /* start a non-blocking transmission */
}

static void on_message(void* context, uint8_t src, uint8_t msg_id, const uint8_t* data,
                       uint8_t length)
{
    (void) context;
    if ((msg_id == BATON_MSG_CMD_SET_OUTPUT) && (length == 2U))
    {
        (void) baton_node_send(&node, src, BATON_MSG_OUTPUT_REPORT, data, 2U, BATON_PRIO_HIGH);
    }
}

void uart_rx_irq_handler(uint8_t byte) /* called by the UART receive interrupt */
{
    baton_node_rx_isr(&node, byte);
}

int main(void)
{
    struct baton_node_config config;
    uint32_t next_status = 0U;

    baton_node_default_config(&config); /* 9600 bit/s, 250 ms slot, single-wire echo */
    config.own_address = 0x11U;
    config.master_address = 0x01U;
    config.slave_addresses = slaves;
    config.slave_count = 2U;
    config.write = uart_write;
    config.on_message = on_message;
    (void) baton_node_init(&node, &config, board_millis());

    for (;;)
    {
        const uint32_t now = board_millis();

        baton_node_process(&node, now);
        if ((int32_t) (now - next_status) >= 0)
        {
            uint8_t uptime[4];

            baton_put_u32le(uptime, now / 1000U);
            (void) baton_node_publish(&node, BATON_MSG_NODE_STATUS, uptime, 4U);
            next_status += 1000U;
        }
    }
}

board_uart_write() and board_millis() stand for your board's UART driver and tick. The message lists (NODE_STATUS, CMD_SET_OUTPUT, OUTPUT_REPORT) come from baton_user_config.h, shared by every node of the bus. The examples are complete programs for bare metal, Zephyr and a PC serial port.

docs.title: struct baton_node
docs.text: The node state, owned by the caller (normally a static variable). Treat its members as private; their layout may change in a minor version.

docs.title: baton_node_default_config()
docs.text:
void baton_node_default_config(struct baton_node_config* config);

Fills config with zeros and the defaults for 9600 bit/s (slave, slot 250 ms, ACK timeout 20 ms, 1 retry, gap 2 ms, inter-byte timeout 5 ms, TTL 5000 ms, echo on). NULL is ignored.

docs.title: baton_node_init()
docs.text:
int baton_node_init(struct baton_node* node, const struct baton_node_config* config,
                    uint32_t now_ms);
Parameter Description node Node state; cleared and initialized config Configuration; copied now_ms Current time Return When BATON_OK The node is running BATON_ERR_PARAM NULL argument or invalid configuration; the node is not initialized

docs.title: baton_node_process()
docs.text:
void baton_node_process(struct baton_node* node, uint32_t now_ms);

Runs the receive path, the transmitter, the state machine and the housekeeping (TTL, queue release). Call every millisecond from one context. Ignored for a NULL or uninitialized node.

docs.title: baton_node_send()
docs.text:
int baton_node_send(struct baton_node* node, uint8_t dst, uint8_t msg_id, const void* data,
                    uint8_t length, uint8_t priority);
Parameter Description dst Destination address or BATON_ADDR_BROADCAST msg_id An EVENT id data, length Data, copied; data may be NULL when length is 0 priority BATON_PRIO_NORMAL or BATON_PRIO_HIGH Return When BATON_OK Queued BATON_ERR_NOT_INIT NULL or uninitialized node BATON_ERR_PARAM data NULL with length > 0 BATON_ERR_MSG_ID Not an EVENT id BATON_ERR_LEN length above MAX_LEN BATON_ERR_ADDR Unknown destination or the node itself BATON_ERR_FULL No room in the queue

The TTL of the event starts at the time of the last baton_node_process() call.

docs.title: baton_node_publish()
docs.text:
int baton_node_publish(struct baton_node* node, uint8_t msg_id, const void* data,
                       uint8_t length);

Stores the new value of a STATE and marks it for every other node. Returns BATON_OK, BATON_ERR_NOT_INIT, BATON_ERR_PARAM, BATON_ERR_MSG_ID (not a STATE id) or BATON_ERR_LEN; never fails for lack of space.

docs.title: baton_node_rx_isr(), baton_node_tx_done_isr()
docs.text:
void baton_node_rx_isr(struct baton_node* node, uint8_t byte);
void baton_node_tx_done_isr(struct baton_node* node);

Interrupt entry points: store a received byte (counted in rx_overflows when the ring is full); signal the end of a transmission when rx_echo is false. NULL is ignored.

docs.text:
void baton_node_get_stats(const struct baton_node* node, struct baton_stats* stats);

Copies the counters; nothing is written when an argument is NULL.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text: This chapter explains how Baton-C is built: the layers and what each one owns, how bytes travel through them, how events and states are stored and packed, the state machines, the memory model, error handling, threading, and the design decisions behind them.

docs.title: Layers
docs.text:
Layer Files Contents Configuration inc/baton_config.h, application baton_user_config.h Sizes (each #ifndef-guarded and range-checked with #error) and the two message lists Definitions inc/baton_defs.h Frame layout, frame types, ACKB bits, static inline CTRL and byte-order helpers. No state Codec inc/baton_protocol.h, src/baton_protocol.c CRC-16, the incremental parser, the encoder. Pure functions over caller buffers Link inc/baton_link.h, src/baton_link.c Receive ring (interrupt producer), parser with inter-byte timeout, transmitter: bus gap, echo check, timeout. Reports events to the node Event queue inc/baton_queue.h, src/baton_queue.c Ring of variable-size records with a serialized 16-byte header Node inc/baton_node.h, src/baton_node.c Master and slave state machines, channels, TLV packing, duplicate filter, TTL, the application API Umbrella baton.h Includes everything; version fallbacks

Each layer depends only on the ones below it. The application normally uses only the eight baton_node_* functions; the codec is public so that tools (a bus monitor, a test generator) can use it alone.

docs.title: Data flow
docs.text:
Receive. The UART interrupt calls baton_node_rx_isr(), which only writes the byte into the ring of the link (single producer, single consumer, no lock). In baton_node_process() the link drains the ring: bytes of the node's own transmission are compared with what was sent (echo), every other byte goes to the parser. A complete valid frame is reported to the node, which dispatches it by type, filters retransmissions and calls on_message once per message.

Transmit. baton_node_send() copies an event into a queue and returns. When the node may transmit — a slave in its slot, the master at the start of a slot — it packs messages for one peer into the payload area of its transmit buffer, baton_encode() adds the header and the CRC in place, and the link calls the write function once the bus has been silent for tx_gap_ms. The transmission ends with the last echo byte (rx_echo) or baton_node_tx_done_isr().

docs.title: The parser
docs.text: The parser is described byte by byte in Protocol → Parser behavior. It decodes into its own struct baton_frame, so no second frame buffer exists, and it computes the CRC while the bytes arrive. The link adds the inter-byte timeout: when more than inter_byte_timeout_ms pass inside a frame, the parser is reset and rx_timeouts counts it.

docs.title: The encoder
docs.text: baton_encode() writes SYNC, the header, the payload and the CRC into a caller buffer after checking the capacity. When the payload already sits at &output[BATON_HEADER_SIZE] — the node packs it there — nothing is copied.

docs.title: Event queues
docs.text:
There are two queues, HIGH and NORMAL. Each is a byte array inside struct baton_node holding variable-size records: a 16-byte header — pending mask, inflight mask, time stamp, id, length, destination, flags, serialized byte by byte (no pointer casts) — and the data, padded to 4 bytes.

  • Copy in. baton_node_send() copies the data and returns at once; the caller keeps no buffer.
  • No split records. A record that does not fit at the end of the array goes to the start; a SKIP marker is left at the end if a header fits there. Data is always contiguous.
  • pending is the node mask still to acknowledge the event; a broadcast sets every other node. inflight is the node mask with an unacknowledged frame containing it; it is always a subset of pending.
  • Release from the head only, when pending is empty. References held by channels therefore stay valid.
  • Peek and commit. Packing does not remove a record; the acknowledgement does, and a retransmission needs no copy.
  • TTL. Every 10 ms records older than event_ttl_ms are removed and reported through on_drop.

An unreachable destination can hold a record at the head of a queue for at most event_ttl_ms; size the queues for the traffic of that time.

docs.title: State mailboxes
docs.text: Each state has a buffer of its MAX_LEN, a current length and a dirty node mask. baton_node_publish() overwrites the value and marks every other node — it never fails for lack of space. Packing copies the current value and clears the destination's bit; if the frame is not acknowledged, the retransmission carries the latest value again. Intermediate values may be skipped; the last one always arrives.

docs.title: Packing a frame
docs.text:
1. If the channel to the peer has an unacknowledged frame, the same messages are packed again with the same SEQ. A state that grew and no longer fits is removed from it and sent later.
  2. Otherwise the frame is filled with the peer's HIGH events in FIFO order up to the first that does not fit, then NORMAL events the same way, then its dirty states.
  3. The limits are the remaining slot budget (Protocol → Time budget), the room of the frame type and BATON_MAX_MSGS_PER_FRAME.

docs.title: State machines
docs.text:
The slave serves its peers in two passes per slot: first the reachable ones in round-robin order, then the ones with three or more failures in a row, once each and without retry. A peer that failed in the slot is in the NACK mask and is not served again in that slot.

The transmitter of the link has three states: idle, waiting for a silent bus, and busy. Busy ends with the full echo (rx_echo) or the TX-done interrupt; a timeout of F(length) + tx_gap_ms + 5 ms is the safety net (tx_timeouts). An echo mismatch is counted in collisions.

docs.title: Memory model
docs.text: All state lives in one caller-owned struct baton_node; the library has no global variables (only static const tables). Its size is fixed at build time by baton_user_config.h — see Configuration → Memory footprint. No function allocates memory, recurses or uses variable-length arrays, so the stack is fixed: see Configuration → Stack usage.

docs.title: Error handling
docs.text: Situation What happens Visible as Invalid argument The function returns an error code and changes nothing BATON_ERR_*, BATON_PARSE_ERROR Inconsistent configuration baton_node_init() fails; the node stays uninitialized BATON_ERR_PARAM Event queue full baton_node_send() fails; nothing is queued BATON_ERR_FULL, queue_full CRC mismatch, LEN too large Frame dropped crc_errors Gap inside a frame Frame dropped, parser reset rx_timeouts Receive ring full Byte dropped rx_overflows Echo differs from the sent bytes Transmission completes, counted collisions Write fails or no end of transmission Treated as sent, counted tx_timeouts No ACK Retry, then NACK in the RESP ack_timeouts, retries No RESP Next slave resp_timeouts, on_poll_done(responded = false) Retransmitted content Acknowledged, not delivered duplicates Unknown or too long message Skipped bad_messages Event older than event_ttl_ms Removed events_dropped, on_drop

docs.title: Threading and reentrancy
docs.text:
Function Context baton_node_process(), baton_node_init(), baton_node_get_stats() One context: the main loop or one RTOS task baton_node_rx_isr() UART receive interrupt; writes only the ring baton_node_tx_done_isr() UART TX-complete interrupt; sets a flag baton_node_send(), baton_node_publish() Any context if enter_critical/exit_critical are set; otherwise the context of baton_node_process() on_message, on_drop, on_poll_done Always inside baton_node_process(); they may call baton_node_send() and baton_node_publish()

Critical sections are a few instructions long: reserving queue space, moving head and tail, copying a state value. Event data is copied outside them. The codec functions are reentrant on different structures. Several buses need several struct baton_node instances; they do not share anything.

docs.title: Design decisions
docs.text: Decision Reason POLL as a token (the baton) Determinism without arbitration: no collisions, a bounded cycle computed from the configuration Two message classes Events need exactly-once, in-order delivery; states need "latest value wins" and must never overflow Several messages per frame (TLV), one ACK per frame At 9600 bit/s the 7-byte overhead and the turnaround dominate; packing removes most of it Traffic with the master has no separate ACK Slave → master content is acknowledged by the ACKB of the next POLL, master → slave content by the ACKB of the RESP in the same slot Stop-and-wait per channel, 4-bit SEQ and FIRST Simple, exactly-once with one outstanding frame; FIRST survives a restart of the sender Retransmission rebuilt from queue references No per-frame copy in RAM Only RESP frames with content are acknowledged An empty RESP shared the SEQ of the next one and confirmed it in advance; the bus simulation found this, the fix is permanent Unreachable nodes served last, polled every 4th cycle A dead node cannot eat the slot or the cycle of the healthy ones on_drop reports the nodes that did not acknowledge No silent loss: the application knows what may be missing Explicit now_ms, no clock reads Portable, testable with simulated time No broadcast frame with slotted ACKs It would be more efficient with many receivers but much more complex; kept for a future major version

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: All notable changes to Baton-C are listed here. The format follows Keep a Changelog and the project uses Semantic Versioning: the public API in baton.h and inc/ and the wire format stay compatible within a major version.

docs.title: Unreleased
docs.text: First public version, prepared for the release 1.0.0. Baton-C continues the internal intercom library (C99, single static instance, Intercom_* API) under a new name, API and repository layout; the wire format and the delivery rules are unchanged.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Layered library: definitions (baton_defs.h), codec (baton_protocol: CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE, incremental parser, in-place encoder), half-duplex link (baton_link: receive ring, inter-byte timeout, bus gap, echo check, transmit timeout), event queue (baton_queue) and node (baton_node: master/slave schedule, TLV packing, stop-and-wait channels, duplicate filter, TTL).
  • Instance-based application API baton_node_* on a caller-owned struct baton_node; several buses in one program; explicit now_ms instead of a clock callback.
  • Compile-time checks of the message lists: unique IDs, message lengths, queue capacity.
  • Unit tests (GoogleTest, 132 tests) with the bus simulation as test cases, a multi-seed simulation runner (baton_sim, tests/run_seeds.*), and integration tests with a Python twin of the codec and a C/Python cross-check.
  • Examples: bare-metal slave (runs in CI against a simulated bus with line noise), PC serial-port master (Linux, macOS, Windows), Zephyr slave.
  • Documentation website (MkDocs Material) with the protocol specification, guides, measured memory, code size and stack, API reference, MISRA C:2012 page, and a printable PDF user manual; generated diagrams (tools/docs/diagrams.py) and a stack analysis script (tools/docs/stack_usage.py).
  • CI workflows: build, unit tests with the coverage gate, integration tests, static analysis (Cppcheck, MISRA, CodeQL), format check, static library, documentation, SBOM and release.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• C11 instead of C99; include/Intercom.h replaced by baton.h and inc/; IntercomConfig.h replaced by baton_user_config.h (BATON_* macros); CMake target baton in baton.cmake, presets BATON[...].
  • Queue records are serialized byte by byte (no pointer casts); every function has a single exit point (MISRA C:2012).

docs.title: Quality
docs.text:
• MISRA C:2012: 0 violations reported by the Cppcheck addon; four deviations recorded in docs/misra.md. CI fails on any violation.
  • 100 % line and branch coverage of src/, enforced by the coverage target.
  • Code size 6620 B and 280 B of worst-case stack on Cortex-M4 (-Os), 1696 B of RAM per node with the configuration template.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: This chapter lists the build-time parameters with their ranges, the derived sizes, the measured memory footprint, code size and stack usage, how to measure them again, and the CMake options. The runtime parameters are described in Using the Library → Set up a node.

docs.title: Build-time parameters
docs.text:
The application defines them in baton_user_config.h (or with -D compiler options); inc/baton_config.h provides the defaults and rejects values out of range with #error.

Macro Default Range Meaning BATON_MAX_NODES 8 2..32 Nodes on the bus including the master BATON_MAX_PAYLOAD 64 16..250 Largest frame payload in bytes BATON_MAX_MSGS_PER_FRAME 16 1..64 Messages packed into one frame BATON_QUEUE_HIGH_SIZE 256 64..65532 HIGH event queue in bytes BATON_QUEUE_NORMAL_SIZE 512 64..65532 NORMAL event queue in bytes BATON_RX_BUF_SIZE 128 16..4096, power of two Receive ring filled by the interrupt BATON_STATE_LIST(X) — required STATE messages X(NAME, ID, MAX_LEN) BATON_EVENT_LIST(X) — required EVENT messages X(NAME, ID, MAX_LEN)

docs.title: Derived sizes
docs.text:
Macro Value Meaning BATON_FRAME_MAX 7 + BATON_MAX_PAYLOAD Largest frame on the wire BATON_MASK_BYTES (BATON_MAX_NODES + 7) / 8 NACK mask in a RESP BATON_RESP_PREFIX 1 + BATON_MASK_BYTES ACKB and NACK BATON_MAX_MSG_LEN BATON_MAX_PAYLOAD − BATON_RESP_PREFIX − 2 Largest MAX_LEN of a message BATON_STATE_COUNT, BATON_EVENT_COUNT from the lists Number of messages BATON_STATE_DATA_SIZE 1 + Σ MAX_LEN of the states State mailboxes

Sizing hints: an event occupies 16 + MAX(len rounded up to 4) bytes of its queue until every destination acknowledged it, at most for event_ttl_ms. The receive ring must hold the bytes that arrive between two calls of baton_node_process() plus the echo of a maximum frame (BATON_FRAME_MAX).

docs.title: Memory footprint
docs.text:
All memory of a node is the caller's struct baton_node; the library has no global or static variables except constant tables. Measured with sizeof for Arm Cortex-M4 (arm-none-eabi-gcc 15.2.1):

Configuration struct baton_node of which queues of which link (ring, parser, counters) Template (8 nodes, payload 64, 16 msgs, queues 256 + 512, ring 128) 1696 B 768 B 280 B Unit tests (as template, ring 256) 1824 B 768 B 408 B Examples (4 nodes, payload 64, 8 msgs, queues 128 + 256, ring 128) 1068 B 384 B 280 B

Approximately: BATON_RX_BUF_SIZE + BATON_QUEUE_HIGH_SIZE + BATON_QUEUE_NORMAL_SIZE + 2 × BATON_FRAME_MAX + 7 + BATON_MAX_NODES × (2 × BATON_MAX_MSGS_PER_FRAME + 10) + state mailboxes + about 300 B of configuration copy, counters and state variables.

docs.title: Code size
docs.text:
Library code (text) for Cortex-M4 Thumb-2, compiled with the configuration template, -ffunction-sections, without the C library functions memcpy, memset and memmove that the library calls:

File -Os -O0 baton_protocol.c 932 B 1070 B baton_link.c 602 B 1376 B baton_queue.c 456 B 1194 B baton_node.c 4630 B 9094 B Total 6620 B 12734 B

The library has no initialized or zero-initialized data of its own (data and bss are 0).

docs.title: Stack usage
docs.text:
Worst-case stack of the entry points, from GCC -fstack-usage -fcallgraph-info=su, following every direct call. Not included: the application functions the library calls through pointers (write, enter_critical, exit_critical, on_message, on_drop, on_poll_done) — add their own stack to the figure of the function that calls them — and memcpy/memset/memmove.

Function Cortex-M4 -Os Cortex-M4 -O0 x86-64 -O2 baton_node_process() 280 B 400 B 752 B baton_node_init() 80 B 160 B 216 B baton_node_send() 80 B 112 B 136 B baton_node_publish() 24 B 64 B 80 B baton_node_get_stats() 24 B 56 B 72 B baton_node_rx_isr() 8 B 40 B 16 B baton_node_tx_done_isr() 0 B 32 B 16 B baton_parser_feed() 24 B 72 B 16 B baton_encode() 48 B 80 B 80 B

Toolchains: Arm GNU Toolchain 15.2.Rel1 (arm-none-eabi-gcc 15.2.1, -mcpu=cortex-m4 -mthumb), MinGW-w64 GCC 14.2.0 (x86-64 Windows ABI, which reserves 32 bytes of shadow space per call).

Worst-case chains:

  • baton_node_process() (-Os): process → slave slot step → DATA frame → pack → state copy → TLV emit, on the reception of a POLL.
  • baton_node_process() (-O0): process → frame dispatch → POLL handler → slot step → RESP → pack → retransmission → state copy → TLV emit.

An interrupt that calls baton_node_rx_isr() adds 8 B (Cortex-M4 -Os) to the stack of whatever it interrupts.

docs.title: How to measure again
docs.text:
mkdir -p build/stack
for f in src/*.c; do
  arm-none-eabi-gcc -mcpu=cortex-m4 -mthumb -Os -std=c11 -fstack-usage -fcallgraph-info=su \
    -I. -Iinc -I<folder of baton_user_config.h> -c "$f" -o "build/stack/$(basename "$f" .c).o" \
    -dumpdir build/stack/
done
python tools/docs/stack_usage.py build/stack
arm-none-eabi-size build/stack/*.o

Measure again after any change in src/ that may change a frame, and update this page.

docs.text:
Three examples share one bus definition, examples/config/baton_user_config.h: master 0x01, slaves 0x11 and 0x12, the state NODE_STATUS (uptime in seconds) and the events CMD_SET_OUTPUT and OUTPUT_REPORT.

docs.title: Bare metal
docs.text:
File Content examples/bare_metal/board.h Four board functions: board_init(), board_millis(), board_uart_write(), board_idle(); the application provides app_uart_rx_isr() examples/bare_metal/main.c The slave: configuration, main loop, uptime state, output commands examples/bare_metal/board_host.c board.h on a PC: a simulated single-wire bus with the master and slave 0x12 as further Baton nodes; checks the results

Structure. The UART receive interrupt calls app_uart_rx_isr(), which passes the byte to baton_node_rx_isr(). The main loop calls baton_node_process() every millisecond, publishes NODE_STATUS once per second, and in on_message applies CMD_SET_OUTPUT and answers with an OUTPUT_REPORT event to the sender. Everything runs in the main loop, so no critical section is configured.

On a PC. board_idle() advances a simulated clock by 1 ms and moves one byte per transmitter over the bus; every byte reaches every node, the sender included (echo). Before each of the three requests a burst of line noise — a broken header A5 11 01 00 with an invalid length, and a stray byte — is put on the idle bus. Real output:

bare-metal example: slave 0x11 at 9600 bit/s on a simulated single-wire bus
  1502 ms  master -> 0x11  CMD_SET_OUTPUT output 0 = 0x01 (after line noise)
  1563 ms  master <- 0x11  OUTPUT_REPORT output 0 = 0x01
  2202 ms  0x12   -> 0x11  CMD_SET_OUTPUT output 1 = 0x55 (after line noise)
  2290 ms  0x12   <- 0x11  OUTPUT_REPORT output 1 = 0x55
  3106 ms  master -> 0x11  CMD_SET_OUTPUT output 2 = 0x00 (after line noise)
  3147 ms  master <- 0x11  OUTPUT_REPORT output 2 = 0x00
master: 274 polls (0 without answer), 3 CRC errors, 0 frames aborted by timeout
ok    master got 2 OUTPUT_REPORT events
ok    last report to the master: output 2 = 0x00
ok    slave 0x12 got 1 OUTPUT_REPORT event
ok    report to 0x12: output 1 = 0x55
ok    master sees the uptime state of 0x11
ok    slave 0x12 sees the uptime state of 0x11
ok    no collisions on the bus
EXAMPLE PASSED

The three CRC errors are the three noise bursts (their length byte is invalid).

Porting. Implement board.h for the MCU:

Function Implementation board_init() Clock the UART, configure single-wire half duplex 8N1 at the baud rate, enable the RX interrupt (and the TX interrupt in the driver) board_millis() A 1 ms SysTick counter board_uart_write() Store the buffer and start an interrupt or DMA transmission; return 0 board_idle() __WFI(); the SysTick interrupt wakes the loop every millisecond

docs.title: Host serial master
docs.text:
File Content examples/host_serial/main.c Command-line master baton_master examples/host_serial/serial_port.h Five functions: open, write, read with timeout, close, millisecond clock examples/host_serial/serial_port_posix.c termios implementation (Linux, macOS) examples/host_serial/serial_port_win32.c Win32 implementation

The master polls 0x11 and 0x12, prints every message it receives and, once per second, the number of polls, the answered ones and the CRC errors. Each --set queues a CMD_SET_OUTPUT event. Use --echo with a single-wire adapter that receives its own bytes; without it, the end of serial_write() is taken as the end of the transmission (baton_node_tx_done_isr()). The example has not been run against hardware yet; without an adapter it reports cannot open <port>.

docs.title: Zephyr
docs.text:
File Content examples/zephyr/src/main.c Slave 0x12: UART interrupt driver, one protocol thread examples/zephyr/CMakeLists.txt Includes baton.cmake, links zephyr_interface examples/zephyr/prj.conf Serial, interrupt-driven UART, no heap examples/zephyr/app.overlay.example The chosen node baton,uart 
west build -b <board> examples/zephyr -- -DDTC_OVERLAY_FILE=<board>.overlay

The UART interrupt passes received bytes to baton_node_rx_isr() and feeds the transmit FIFO from the buffer of the write function; the transmission ends with the echo of the last byte (rx_echo). A thread calls baton_node_process() every millisecond and publishes the uptime. enter_critical and exit_critical use irq_lock() so that other threads may send events. Disable the console and logging on the bus UART.

This example is not compiled in this repository (no Zephyr workspace in CI); treat it as a starting point.

docs.title: Extending the Library
docs.text: Almost everything an application needs is done on top of the library: new messages are configuration, new transports are a write function and an interrupt handler, data models are application code. This chapter says where each extension belongs and how to contribute changes to the library itself.

docs.title: Where to extend
docs.text: You want to… Do it in Library change needed? Add a message BATON_STATE_LIST / BATON_EVENT_LIST of baton_user_config.h on every node No Larger frames, more nodes, bigger queues The sizes in baton_user_config.h No Support another UART, RS-485 or a USB adapter The write function and the receive interrupt No Give message data a structure Encode and decode functions in the application No Monitor a bus The codec alone (baton_parser_feed()) No Change timing (slot, timeouts, baud rate) struct baton_node_config No Change the wire format or the delivery rules src/, the Python twin, the protocol chapter Yes — a new major version

docs.title: Adding a message
docs.text:
1. Add X(NAME, ID, MAX_LEN) to the state or event list with a new ID.
  2. Rebuild every node of the bus with the new list. A node with an old list counts the new message in bad_messages and ignores it.
  3. Write an encode and a decode function for its data with an explicit byte order.

Changing the MAX_LEN of a message is compatible as long as the senders never use more than the smallest MAX_LEN among the nodes.

docs.title: Adding a transport
docs.text:
The write function contract:

Requirement Why Start the transmission and return 0, or return a negative value The node never blocks; a failure is counted in tx_timeouts and treated as sent Keep sending from the given buffer The library keeps it unchanged until the end of the transmission End: last echo byte (rx_echo = true) or baton_node_tx_done_isr() The link uses it to start the next timer and to free the bus Called only from baton_node_process() It may use the same resources as the processing context

Received bytes of every node — including the own echo — go to baton_node_rx_isr().

docs.title: Data models
docs.text: Keep the application data out of the library: define, per message, a C structure and two functions that convert it to and from bytes. The examples encode the uptime with baton_put_u32le() and decode it with baton_get_u32le() from baton_defs.h.

docs.title: Several buses
docs.text: Use one struct baton_node per bus. Nodes share nothing, but they share the message lists of the build; buses with different message lists need separate builds of the library (for example two CMake targets with different BATON_CONFIG_DIR).

docs.title: Bridging buses
docs.text: A gateway node is a member of two buses (two struct baton_node) and forwards in its on_message callbacks: an event received on bus A is sent with baton_node_send() on bus B. Delivery is then exactly once per hop; end-to-end confirmation, if needed, is an application message (like OUTPUT_REPORT in the examples).

docs.title: Contributing to the library
docs.text:
1. Code. C11, no new dependencies, no heap, the MISRA rules used in the code (single exit, parenthesized expressions, no pointer arithmetic, (void) on ignored results).
  2. Tests. Every behavior change needs a test; coverage must stay at 100 % lines and branches; the bus simulation must pass on 100 seeds (tests/run_seeds.sh). Update the Python twin when the codec changes.
  3. Analysis. misra-analyze reports 0 violations, or the deviation is recorded in MISRA C:2012.
  4. Format. clang-format reports no changes.
  5. Documentation. The affected pages, the stack and size tables (Configuration), the diagrams (tools/docs/diagrams.py), and CHANGELOG.md under [Unreleased].
  6. Compatibility. The public API and the wire format stay stable within a major version.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: This chapter shows how to get Baton-C, add it to your project, and build, test and analyze it.

docs.title: Get the library
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/AntonVynohradov/Baton-C.git

The usual way to use it is as a Git submodule of the firmware project:

git submodule add https://github.com/AntonVynohradov/Baton-C.git lib/Baton-C

Each release provides the source code, a prebuilt static library for Linux x86-64 with its headers (built with the configuration template), the MISRA report and the PDF user manual.

docs.title: Add it to your project
docs.text:
1. Configuration. Copy config/baton_user_config_template.h into your project as baton_user_config.h, define your message lists and, if needed, the sizes. Every node of a bus must use the same message lists. Do not edit the template inside the submodule.

2a. CMake.

set(BATON_CONFIG_DIR ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/config)   # folder with baton_user_config.h
include(lib/Baton-C/baton.cmake)
target_link_libraries(app PRIVATE baton)

2b. Any other build system (vendor IDE, Make). Compile src/*.c with C11 and add the repository root, inc/ and the folder of your baton_user_config.h to the include path of the library and of the application.

3. Code. Include baton.h, fill a struct baton_node_config and follow Using the Library.

The prebuilt package of a release is compiled with the configuration template; it is useful for host tools with the same message lists. Firmware normally builds the sources with its own configuration.

docs.title: Prerequisites for development
docs.text:
• C11 compiler (GCC or Clang), CMake 3.20+, Make
  • Unit tests: GoogleTest and gcovr
  • Integration tests: Python 3 with pytest, and gcc on the path for the cross-check
  • Analysis: Cppcheck (with its misra.py addon) and optionally the CodeQL CLI
  • Formatting: clang-format
  • Documentation: the packages of requirements-dev.txt (MkDocs Material, mkdoxy, WeasyPrint), Doxygen, and Pango for WeasyPrint

docs.title: Unit tests and coverage
docs.text:
cmake --preset "BATON[UnitTests]"
cmake --build "build/BATON[UnitTests]" --target coverage

The 132 GoogleTest tests cover the codec, the link, the queue and both state machines, plus the bus simulation: several nodes on a simulated single-wire bus with the real byte time of 9600 bit/s, bit errors, a dead node and an RS-485 variant without echo. Each scenario checks exactly-once in-order delivery, final state delivery, no collisions and the slot length. The coverage target fails below BATON_COVERAGE_MIN (100 %) line or branch coverage of src/; the HTML report is in build/BATON[UnitTests]/Coverage/.

The same simulation runs optimized for many seeds:

cmake --build "build/BATON[UnitTests]" --target baton_sim
tests/run_seeds.sh "build/BATON[UnitTests]" 100            # Windows: tests\run_seeds.ps1

docs.title: Integration tests
docs.text:
cmake --preset "BATON[IntegrationTests]"
cmake --build "build/BATON[IntegrationTests]" --target integration_tests

tests/integration/baton/protocol.py is an independent Python implementation of the codec using only the standard library (the Python twin). The tests check the reference frames of the protocol chapter, and compile src/baton_protocol.c with gcc to compare 300 random frames between C and Python — encoding, parsing, and the reaction to a corrupted byte. Without gcc the cross-check is skipped and pytest says so. When CMake finds a Python without pytest, pass -DPython3_EXECUTABLE=<python with pytest>.

docs.title: Formatting
docs.text:
clang-format -i baton.h src/*.c inc/*.h tests/unit/*.cpp tests/unit/*.h tests/sim/*.[ch] examples/*/*.[ch]

.clang-format is LLVM-based: 4 spaces, Allman braces, 100 columns, pointer to the type. The Format Check workflow fails a pull request that changes under clang-format.

docs.title: Versioning and releases
docs.text:
The version comes from the latest vX.Y.Z Git tag (cmake/version.cmake); without a tag, BATON_DEFAULT_VERSION is used. baton.h has the same fallbacks for builds without CMake, and a unit test checks that BATON_VERSION matches the numbers. A release:

  1. Set BATON_DEFAULT_VERSION and the fallbacks in baton.h to X.Y.Z.
  2. Move the [Unreleased] entries of CHANGELOG.md to ## [X.Y.Z] - YYYY-MM-DD.
  3. Merge to main; the maintainer tags and pushes vX.Y.Z.

The Release workflow checks that the tag, baton.h, cmake/version.cmake and the changelog agree, runs every gate (coverage, integration, MISRA, examples), builds the package, the MISRA report and the PDF manual, and publishes the GitHub release.

docs.title: Integration Guide
docs.text:
The library does not touch hardware. An integration has three parts:

  1. Receive: the UART receive interrupt passes every byte to baton_node_rx_isr(). It only writes the ring of the node, so it is safe in an interrupt.
  2. Transmit: a write function that starts sending a complete frame and returns, plus — without echo — a call of baton_node_tx_done_isr() when the last byte left.
  3. Processing and application: one context calls baton_node_process() every millisecond with the current time; the callbacks run there.

Complete, buildable programs for each pattern are described in Examples.

docs.title: The physical layer
docs.text:
Wiring rx_echo Notes Single wire: TX and RX on one pin (STM32 half-duplex mode, or open-drain TX tied to RX) true The receiver hears every transmitted byte; the library compares the echo and ends the transmission with the last echo byte Open-drain bus with pull-up, separate TX and RX pins tied together true Same as above RS-485 with automatic or GPIO direction control, receiver disabled while sending false Call baton_node_tx_done_isr() from the TX-complete (shift register empty) interrupt, after switching the transceiver back to receive RS-485 with the receiver always enabled true The echo also detects a transceiver that drives too late or too long

Keep the line idle-high, 8N1, the same baud rate on every node. The turnaround time of a transceiver must be shorter than tx_gap_ms.

docs.title: Bare metal
docs.text:
void USART1_IRQHandler(void) /* example names for an STM32 */
{
    if (usart_rx_not_empty())
    {
        baton_node_rx_isr(&node, usart_read_byte());
    }
    if (usart_tx_empty() && (tx_position < tx_length))
    {
        usart_write_byte(tx_buffer[tx_position]);
        tx_position++;
    }
}

The write function stores the pointer and the length and enables the TX-empty interrupt; the library keeps the buffer valid until the end of the transmission. The main loop calls baton_node_process(&node, millis) every millisecond (SysTick). When baton_node_send() is also called from another interrupt, set enter_critical and exit_critical to disable and restore interrupts (__disable_irq() / restore the previous PRIMASK).

docs.title: RTOS
docs.text:
Part Where baton_node_rx_isr(), baton_node_tx_done_isr() UART interrupt handler; no RTOS call needed, the ring is lock-free baton_node_process() One task with a 1 ms period (vTaskDelayUntil, k_sleep(K_MSEC(1))) at a priority above the application tasks that wait for bus data baton_node_send(), baton_node_publish() Any task, with enter_critical/exit_critical set to a short interrupt lock (irq_lock(), taskENTER_CRITICAL()) Callbacks Run in the protocol task; post to a queue of the application task for longer work

The critical section must exclude the UART interrupt and every other context that calls send or publish. A mutex is not enough when an interrupt is one of them.

docs.title: Adding the library to a CMake build
docs.text:
set(BATON_CONFIG_DIR ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/config)   # folder with baton_user_config.h
include(path/to/Baton-C/baton.cmake)
target_link_libraries(app PRIVATE baton)
target_link_libraries(baton PUBLIC zephyr_interface)       # Zephyr applications only

baton.cmake defines the static library target baton with its include directories (the repository root, inc/ and BATON_CONFIG_DIR) and the version definitions. For a Zephyr application, linking zephyr_interface compiles the library with the board's architecture flags.

Without CMake: compile src/baton_protocol.c, src/baton_link.c, src/baton_queue.c and src/baton_node.c with C11 and the three include folders.

docs.title: Host
docs.text: On a PC or a Linux board the master or a monitor reads the serial port with a short timeout and passes the bytes to baton_node_rx_isr() from the same thread that calls baton_node_process(). A blocking write is acceptable there; call baton_node_tx_done_isr() after it returns when the adapter has no echo. USB-UART adapters add latency (often 1–16 ms); keep tx_gap_ms and ack_timeout_ms above it.

docs.title: Hardware bring-up
docs.text:
Baton-C has been verified on a simulated bus (unit tests, the bus simulation with noise and a dead node, the bare-metal example on a simulated board); it has not yet been tested on hardware. When bringing it up:

  1. Check the line with a logic analyzer: idle high, 8N1, the configured baud rate, and the first POLL A5 11 01 20 01 00 7C 44 (master 0x01 polling 0x11).
  2. Start with the master and one slave; on_poll_done must report responded.
  3. Check collisions (must stay 0) and tx_timeouts on every node — they reveal a wrong rx_echo setting or a transceiver that switches too late.
  4. Add the other slaves and confirm the cycle time against Protocol → Time budget.
  5. Pull the cable of one slave: the others must keep their slots, and on_drop must report the events to it after event_ttl_ms.

docs.title: MISRA C:2012 compliance
docs.text: This page records how the library is checked against MISRA C:2012 and every deviation from it. It covers the library code only: src/, inc/ and baton.h. Tests, examples and tools are not in scope.

docs.title: Checking
docs.text:
Check Where Gate Cppcheck MISRA C:2012 addon misra-analyze target, CI job MISRA C:2012 Analysis Fails on any violation Cppcheck, all checks cppcheck-analyze target, CI job Cppcheck Analysis Report CodeQL cpp-queries codeql-analyze target, CI job CodeQL Analysis Report Compiler -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Wconversion, -Werror in the test builds No warnings Manual review Pull request review Reviewer

misra-analyze analyzes src/*.c with the configuration tests/config/baton_user_config.h and fails when the report contains a violation. Set -DBATON_MISRA_FAIL_ON_VIOLATION=OFF to get the report without failing. A violation that cannot be fixed must be added to the deviation register below — and, when the addon reports it, suppressed at that line with a cppcheck-suppress comment that names the deviation.

The addon checks most decidable rules, not the directives or the rules that need the whole program or the intent of the code; those are covered by the manual review notes.

docs.text: Item Result Cppcheck MISRA addon (2.16.2) 0 violations; 4 suppressed findings, all DEV-04 Cppcheck, all checks (2.16.2) 0 findings Unit test coverage of src/ 100 % lines (1053), 100 % branches (601) Deviations 4, listed below

docs.title: Manual review notes
docs.text: Guideline How the library complies Dir 4.1 (run-time failures) Every array index is bounded: by a length check, by the configuration invariants checked with #error and _Static_assert (payload, message lengths, queue capacity), or by the parser's own range checks, which also catch a corrupted parser structure. Unsigned time differences wrap by design. Dir 4.11 (validity of arguments) Every public function checks its pointer arguments and lengths. The static inline helpers of baton_defs.h take a pointer to 2 or 4 readable bytes, like memcpy(). Dir 4.12, Rule 21.3 (dynamic memory) No heap. All state is in the caller-owned struct baton_node. Rule 8.9, 8.4 (definitions) Constant tables are static const at the narrowest scope. Rule 11.3, 11.5 (pointer casts) None: queue records are serialized byte by byte instead of casting the byte array to a structure. Rule 15.5 (single point of exit) Every function has one return at the end. Rule 17.2 (recursion) No recursion; the stack is fixed, see Configuration. Rule 21.6 (standard I/O) No <stdio.h>. The library includes only <stddef.h>, <stdint.h>, <stdbool.h> and <string.h>.

docs.title: DEV-01: int as the status type (Dir 4.6, advisory)
docs.text:
• Location: return type of the functions that return a status (baton_node_init(), baton_node_send(), baton_node_publish(), baton_parser_feed(), baton_encode(), baton_link_*()), the baton_write_fn callback, and the internal pack() result.
  • Rationale: the values are status codes, not quantities whose size matters. int lets an integrator pass an existing driver function as baton_write_fn without a wrapper. int has at least 16 bits on every conforming compiler, enough for every value used.
  • Risk control: the library does no arithmetic on status values; it compares them with 0 or with the named constants.

docs.title: DEV-02: macros not used inside the library (Rule 2.5, advisory)
docs.text:
• Location: public constants that only applications and tools use, for example BATON_VERSION_* in baton.h and the generated BATON_MSG_<NAME>_MAX_LEN.
  • Rationale: they are the public names of protocol and API values.

docs.title: DEV-03: external functions referenced in one translation unit (Rule 8.7, advisory)
docs.text:
• Location: the public API functions that the library itself does not call, for example baton_node_get_stats() and baton_crc16().
  • Rationale: they are the library interface; internal linkage would remove them.

docs.title: DEV-04: application message lists as X-macros (Rules 20.7 required, 20.10 and Dir 4.9 advisory)
docs.text:
• Location: BATON_STATE_LIST(X) / BATON_EVENT_LIST(X) in the application's baton_user_config.h (Rule 20.7: the parameter X is used as a macro name, which cannot be parenthesized); BATON_X_MSG_ENUM_ and BATON_X_MSG_SIZE_ in inc/baton_node.h (Rule 20.10: ## builds BATON_MSG_<NAME>); the list macros themselves are function-like macros (Dir 4.9).
  • Rationale: the lists are the single definition of the messages of a bus. From them the library generates, at compile time, the message identifiers, the length table, the state mailbox layout, a switch whose duplicate case values reject duplicate IDs, and _Static_assert checks of every length and of the queue capacity. Writing these by hand would duplicate each message in several places, which is the error the rules aim to prevent.
  • Risk control: the expansion is checked by the compiler (-Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Wconversion -Werror in the tests) and by the compile-time assertions; the generated code is covered by the unit tests; the suppressions name this deviation at each line (cppcheck-suppress misra-c2012-20.7 / 20.10). Applications that run their own MISRA analysis inherit this deviation for their baton_user_config.h.

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text: Baton-C is a C11 library for deterministic master/slave messaging between a few microcontrollers on one shared UART line (single-wire half duplex, open-drain or RS-485, 9600 bit/s by default). The master passes a token — the baton — to each slave in turn; only the node that holds it transmits. On top of this collision-free schedule the library delivers application messages of two kinds: events, delivered exactly once and in order, and states, of which the latest value always arrives. It is written for embedded systems that must be predictable and reviewable: no heap, no RTOS, no clock reads, MISRA C:2012 without violations and 100 % line and branch test coverage.

docs.title: What the library does
docs.text:
• Schedules the bus. The master polls the slaves in a fixed order. A polled slave may send DATA frames to other slaves and must end its slot with a RESP within slot_time_ms. The worst-case cycle depends only on the configuration, not on the traffic.
  • Delivers events reliably. Events are queued (HIGH and NORMAL priority), packed several per frame, acknowledged, retransmitted with the same sequence number, filtered for duplicates, and dropped after event_ttl_ms with a report of the nodes that did not acknowledge them.
  • Delivers states. A state is a mailbox: publishing overwrites it and marks it for every other node. It cannot overflow; intermediate values may be skipped.
  • Handles an unreliable bus. CRC-16 per frame, inter-byte timeout, echo check of the own transmission, retries, and a schedule that keeps unreachable nodes from eating the time of the healthy ones.
  • Encodes and parses frames. The codec can be used on its own, for example in a bus monitor.

docs.title: What the library does not do
docs.text: Concern Why it is not in the library UART driver, pin setup, transceiver direction Hardware-specific; you pass received bytes in and provide a non-blocking write function. Threads, interrupt priorities, locking Every system has its own; the library offers two optional critical-section hooks. See the integration guide. A clock Every call that needs the time takes now_ms; the library never reads a timer. Message meaning, data layouts, units Application data; the library transports byte strings up to their MAX_LEN. Arbitration between several masters One master per bus is the design. Broadcast frames A broadcast event is sent to each node in its own frame and acknowledged by each one (see design decisions).

docs.title: Who it is for
docs.text:
• Small multi-MCU products — a control board and a few sensor, actuator or display boards connected by one wire, where CAN is too expensive and a plain UART protocol has no delivery guarantee.
  • Safety- or certification-minded firmware that needs bounded execution time, static memory and a documented MISRA C:2012 status.
  • Host tools — a PC or a Linux board can be the master or a bus monitor through a USB-UART adapter (see the examples).

docs.title: Key properties
docs.text: Property Value Language C11, no warnings with -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Wconversion Dependencies <stddef.h>, <stdint.h>, <stdbool.h>, <string.h> only Memory No heap, no global variables; all state in a caller-owned struct baton_node RAM per node 1696 B with the configuration template (8 nodes, 64-byte payload, queues 256 + 512 B), details Code size 6620 B on Cortex-M4 with -Os (GCC 15.2), without memcpy/memset/memmove Stack 280 B worst case in baton_node_process() on Cortex-M4 -Os, details Execution time Bounded by the configured sizes; no function blocks or waits Coding standard MISRA C:2012, 0 Cppcheck addon violations, 4 deviations Tests 100 % line and branch coverage; bus simulation with noise and dead nodes; C/Python cross-check Thread safety One processing context plus interrupts; see Threading License Apache License 2.0

docs.title: Terminology
docs.text: Master The node that polls the slaves; node index 0. Exactly one per bus. Slave A node that transmits only while it holds the baton; node index 1..n in the order of slave_addresses, which must be identical on every node. Slot The time between a POLL to a slave and its RESP, at most slot_time_ms. Cycle One round of POLLs over all slaves. Frame One unit on the wire: SYNC DST SRC CTRL LEN PAYLOAD CRC. Types: POLL, RESP, DATA, ACK. Message One application record (id, length, data) inside a frame payload (TLV). Several messages share one frame and one acknowledgement. Event A message class: queued, acknowledged, delivered exactly once, in order. State A message class: a mailbox whose latest value is delivered to every other node. Channel The stop-and-wait state between two nodes in one direction: a 4-bit sequence number, the FIRST flag and the list of messages in the unacknowledged frame. Node mask A 32-bit set of node indexes; bit 0 is the master, bit i is slave_addresses[i - 1].

docs.title: Conventions in this documentation
docs.text:
• Hexadecimal bytes without prefix inside frames (A5 11 01), with 0x in text and code.
  • The CRC is big endian on the wire; node masks inside a RESP are little endian.
  • Sizes are shown with the values of the configuration template (config/baton_user_config_template.h), timing with the defaults of baton_node_default_config() at 9600 bit/s.

docs.title: Baton bus protocol
docs.text: This chapter specifies the Baton bus protocol — the bytes on the wire, the slot schedule and the delivery rules — and says exactly what Baton-C does with each part. It is the specification of the protocol: other implementations (for example the Python twin in tests/integration/baton/protocol.py) are checked against it.

docs.title: The bus
docs.text:
Property Value Medium One shared UART line: single wire (TX and RX on one pin), open-drain, or RS-485 Character format 8N1: 10 bits per byte, 1.04 ms per byte at 9600 bit/s Nodes One master and 1..31 slaves (BATON_MAX_NODES 2..32), addresses 0x00..0xFE Topology Identical on every node: master address and the slave list in polling order Access Only the polled slave transmits, for at most slot_time_ms; other slaves send only ACKs to DATA addressed to them Turnaround Before transmitting, a node waits for tx_gap_ms of silence on the line

The address 0xFF (BATON_ADDR_BROADCAST) is reserved: it selects "every other node" in baton_node_send() and never appears in a frame.

docs.title: Frame
docs.text:
Offset Field Size Description 0 SYNC 1 0xA5, start of a frame 1 DST 1 Destination address 2 SRC 1 Source address 3 CTRL 1 TYPE[7:6], FIRST[5], reserved [4] (0), SEQ[3:0] 4 LEN 1 Number of payload bytes, 0..BATON_MAX_PAYLOAD (at most 250) 5 PAYLOAD LEN Depends on the frame type, see below 5 + LEN CRC16 2 CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE over DST..PAYLOAD, high byte first

The overhead is 7 bytes. An ACK (no payload) takes 7 bytes, 8 ms at 9600 bit/s; a maximum frame with the default 64-byte payload takes 71 bytes, 74 ms.

docs.title: Checksum
docs.text: CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE: polynomial 0x1021, initial value 0xFFFF, no reflection, no final XOR. It covers DST, SRC, CTRL, LEN and the payload — not SYNC. The check value of the catalogue ("123456789") is 0x29B1; it is a unit test. Baton-C computes it bit by bit without a table (no 512-byte table in flash; at 9600 bit/s the cost does not matter).

docs.title: Frame types and payloads
docs.text:
TYPE Name Direction Payload 0 POLL master → slave ACKB, then messages for this slave 1 RESP slave → master ACKB, NACK mask, then messages for the master 2 DATA slave → slave Messages for the destination 3 ACK slave → slave None; SEQ in CTRL is the acknowledged sequence number
  • ACKB (1 byte): bit 7 = valid, bits 3..0 = acknowledged sequence number. In a POLL it acknowledges the last RESP with content from this slave; in a RESP it acknowledges the POLL that started the slot.
  • NACK ((BATON_MAX_NODES + 7) / 8 bytes, little endian): the node mask of the slaves that did not acknowledge a DATA frame of this slave in this slot.

docs.title: Messages (TLV)
docs.text: A payload carries messages back to back, each as ID, LEN, DATA[LEN]. One frame carries up to BATON_MAX_MSGS_PER_FRAME messages. The receiver checks every ID and LEN against the message lists of baton_user_config.h; an unknown id or a length above the MAX_LEN of the message is skipped and counted in bad_messages, a truncated record ends the payload. The largest MAX_LEN is BATON_MAX_MSG_LEN = BATON_MAX_PAYLOAD − 3 − BATON_MASK_BYTES, so that one message fits into every frame type.

docs.title: Parser behavior
docs.text:
baton_parser_feed() takes one byte per call:

  1. Between frames it waits for 0xA5; other bytes are ignored.
  2. It stores DST, SRC, CTRL and LEN, updating the CRC register with each byte.
  3. A LEN above BATON_MAX_PAYLOAD is rejected as soon as it is read: return BATON_PARSE_ERROR, wait for SYNC.
  4. It stores LEN payload bytes, then the two CRC bytes.
  5. A matching CRC returns 1 (the frame is in parser->frame); a mismatch returns BATON_PARSE_ERROR. Either way the parser waits for the next SYNC.

Recovery: the bytes of a rejected frame are not scanned again for a SYNC byte. The link resets the parser when more than inter_byte_timeout_ms pass between two bytes of a frame, so a frame cut off by noise costs at most that timeout. A corrupted parser structure (state or index out of range) is detected and reset instead of writing out of bounds; this is a unit test.

docs.title: The slot
docs.text:
1. The master sends a POLL to the next slave in slave_addresses, carrying the master's messages for it.
  2. The polled slave owns the slot. For every other slave with pending messages it:
    • packs them into a DATA frame that fits the remaining time budget,
    • waits up to ack_timeout_ms for the ACK and retries up to max_retries times,
    • after an ACK, serves the same peer again if it has more.
  3. Finally the slave sends a RESP: it acknowledges the POLL, reports the NACK mask and carries messages for the master.
  4. The master moves on after the RESP or after a timeout.

Each slot starts with a different peer (round robin), so no slave is always served last.

docs.title: Stop-and-wait per channel
docs.text:
Every ordered pair of nodes has an independent channel with a 4-bit sequence number:

  • A sender has at most one unacknowledged frame with content per channel.
  • A retransmission has the same SEQ and the same messages. It is rebuilt from references into the queue, so no copy of the frame is kept.
  • SEQ advances only after an acknowledgement: an ACK, the ACKB of a RESP, or the ACKB of a POLL.
  • The receiver remembers the last accepted SEQ of each sender. A frame with the same number is acknowledged again but not delivered, and counted in duplicates. Events are therefore delivered exactly once.
  • Frames without content (POLL or RESP without messages) do not take part in sequencing: the receiver does not filter them, and the master does not acknowledge an empty RESP. An empty frame therefore never acknowledges the next frame with content in advance.

docs.title: FIRST flag
docs.text: After baton_node_init() a sender sets FIRST in each channel until its first acknowledgement. A receiver accepts a FIRST frame even when its SEQ equals the last accepted one, unless that one was also a FIRST frame with the same SEQ (a retransmission). A sender that restarts is therefore not mistaken for a duplicate.

docs.title: Order
docs.text: Events from one sender to one destination with the same priority arrive in the order they were sent: packing never skips a message of a queue. HIGH events may overtake NORMAL ones.

docs.title: Abandoned content
docs.text: When every event of an unacknowledged frame expired (TTL), the channel advances SEQ, so new content is not mistaken for a duplicate.

docs.title: Unreachable nodes
docs.text:
Situation Behavior A slave does not acknowledge DATA Its bit goes into the NACK mask of the RESP; the failure streak of the channel grows 3 failures in a row (BATON_DEAD_STREAK) The peer is served last in the slot, once, without retry A slave does not answer 3 POLLs in a row The master polls it only every 4th cycle (BATON_DEAD_POLL_DIV) An event is not delivered within event_ttl_ms Removed; on_drop(msg_id, dst, missed_nodes)

The first acknowledgement resets the failure streak. missed_nodes lists the nodes that did not acknowledge the event: a node may still have received it when only its ACK was lost. The reverse never happens — every loss is reported.

docs.title: Time budget
docs.text:
F(n) is the duration of an n-byte frame, ⌈n · 10000 / baudrate⌉ ms; Fmax = F(7 + BATON_MAX_PAYLOAD).

Slave. A DATA frame is started only if an ACK and a maximum RESP still fit:

available_ms = slot_time_ms − elapsed − (Fmax + 2·tx_gap_ms + 2) − tx_gap_ms − ack_timeout_ms
max_payload  = min(available_ms · baudrate / 10000 − 7, BATON_MAX_PAYLOAD)

The RESP therefore always ends within slot_time_ms after the POLL, whatever the number of peers and retries.

Master. It waits for the RESP slot_time_ms + tx_gap_ms + 10 ms after the end of the POLL. If a frame is being received at that moment it waits for its end, but at most twice as long.

Checked by baton_node_init():

slot_time_ms   ≥ Fmax + 3·tx_gap_ms + 2 + ack_timeout_ms + F(7 + 2 + BATON_MAX_MSG_LEN)
ack_timeout_ms > F(7) + tx_gap_ms

For the defaults (9600 bit/s, 64-byte payload, gap 2 ms, ACK timeout 20 ms, slot 250 ms):

Quantity Value Maximum frame (71 bytes) 74 ms ACK (7 bytes) 8 ms Minimum slot 174 ms Empty slot (POLL 8 bytes + RESP 9 bytes + gaps) about 25 ms Longest slot, POLL included at most 74 + 2 + 250 + 12 ≈ 340 ms Longest cycle with N slaves about N × 340 ms

The longest cycle depends only on the configuration. Heavy traffic makes messages wait longer in the queues; it does not make a slot longer.

docs.title: Using the Library
docs.text: This chapter shows how to set up a node, write a slave and a master, send events and publish states, read the diagnostics, use the codec on its own, and avoid the common mistakes. The complete programs are in the examples.

docs.title: Define the messages
docs.text:
Every node of a bus is built with the same baton_user_config.h. Each message is X(NAME, ID, MAX_LEN); the library generates BATON_MSG_<NAME> (the id) and BATON_MSG_<NAME>_MAX_LEN:

#define BATON_STATE_LIST(X)                                                                        \
    X(NODE_STATUS, 0x01, 4)                                                                        \
    X(TEMPERATURE, 0x02, 2)

#define BATON_EVENT_LIST(X)                                                                        \
    X(CMD_START, 0x10, 8)                                                                          \
    X(CMD_STOP, 0x11, 1)                                                                           \
    X(ALARM, 0x12, 16)
Rule Checked IDs 0..255, unique across both lists At compile time (duplicate case value, _Static_assert) MAX_LEN 1..BATON_MAX_MSG_LEN At compile time Each event fits into both queues At compile time Same lists on every node Not checkable — a mismatch shows as bad_messages

Use a state for a value whose latest version matters (a measurement, a mode, a heartbeat); use an event for something that must happen exactly once (a command, an alarm, a button press).

docs.title: Set up a node
docs.text:
static const uint8_t slaves[] = {0x11U, 0x12U, 0x13U}; /* polling order, same on every node */
static struct baton_node node;

int start_node(void)
{
    struct baton_node_config config;

    baton_node_default_config(&config);
    config.role = BATON_ROLE_SLAVE;
    config.own_address = 0x12U;
    config.master_address = 0x01U;
    config.slave_addresses = slaves;
    config.slave_count = 3U;
    config.write = uart_write;
    config.on_message = on_message;
    return baton_node_init(&node, &config, board_millis());
}
Field Default Meaning role BATON_ROLE_SLAVE BATON_ROLE_MASTER or BATON_ROLE_SLAVE own_address, master_address — The master uses own_address == master_address slave_addresses, slave_count — Slaves in polling order, 1..BATON_MAX_NODES − 1; the array must stay valid baudrate 9600 Used for frame durations and the slot budget slot_time_ms 250 Longest slot; at least the minimum checked by init ack_timeout_ms 20 Wait for an ACK after DATA max_retries 1 DATA retransmissions per slot tx_gap_ms 2 Silence before transmitting inter_byte_timeout_ms 5 Gap that aborts a frame cycle_period_ms 0 Master: shortest time between cycle starts event_ttl_ms 5000 Undelivered events are dropped after this; 0 = never rx_echo true The UART receives its own bytes (single wire); false for RS-485 without echo write — Starts a non-blocking transmission (required) enter_critical, exit_critical NULL Both or neither; needed to call send/publish from other contexts on_message, on_drop, on_poll_done NULL Callbacks, called from baton_node_process() context NULL Passed to every hook and callback

baton_node_init() returns BATON_ERR_PARAM for an inconsistent configuration: a missing write function, a broadcast or duplicate address, own_address not on the bus or not matching the role, a slot shorter than one maximum exchange, an ACK timeout not longer than an ACK frame plus the gap. It can be called again to restart the node.

docs.title: The write function
docs.text:
static int uart_write(void* context, const uint8_t* data, size_t length)
{
    (void) context;
    return board_uart_write(data, length); /* 0 = started, negative = failed */
}

The function starts the transmission and returns; the bytes go out from the TX interrupt or a DMA channel. The buffer stays valid until the transmission ends: with rx_echo the library sees its last byte come back; otherwise call baton_node_tx_done_isr() from the TX-complete interrupt. A blocking write also works (see the host example), but it delays the processing of received bytes by the duration of the frame.

docs.title: Run the node
docs.text:
void uart_rx_irq_handler(uint8_t byte)
{
    baton_node_rx_isr(&node, byte);
}

void main_loop(void)
{
    for (;;)
    {
        baton_node_process(&node, board_millis());
        board_wait_for_tick(); /* about 1 ms */
    }
}

Call baton_node_process() at least every millisecond; it never blocks. All timing — gaps, timeouts, the slot budget, TTL — is measured with the now_ms you pass, a monotonic millisecond counter that may wrap.

docs.title: Write a slave
docs.text:
A slave reacts to the messages it receives and publishes its own:

static void on_message(void* context, uint8_t src, uint8_t msg_id, const uint8_t* data,
                       uint8_t length)
{
    (void) context;
    (void) src;
    if ((msg_id == BATON_MSG_CMD_STOP) && (length == 1U))
    {
        motor_stop(data[0]);
    }
}

void report_temperature(int16_t centi_degrees)
{
    uint8_t value[2];

    value[0] = (uint8_t) ((uint16_t) centi_degrees & 0xFFU);
    value[1] = (uint8_t) ((uint16_t) centi_degrees >> 8);
    (void) baton_node_publish(&node, BATON_MSG_TEMPERATURE, value, 2U);
}

Rules of a well-behaved slave:

  • Keep on_message short; it runs inside baton_node_process(). Queue longer work.
  • Encode data with an explicit byte order (as above), not by copying structs: every node must agree on the layout.
  • Expect a message more than once only if it is a state (a new value) — events arrive exactly once.

docs.title: Write a master
docs.text:
The master runs the schedule by itself; its application sends and receives like a slave and may watch the slots:

static void on_poll_done(void* context, uint8_t slave, bool responded, uint32_t nack_nodes)
{
    (void) context;
    if (!responded)
    {
        mark_offline(slave); /* no RESP in this slot */
    }
    if (nack_nodes != 0U)
    {
        log_unreachable(slave, nack_nodes); /* the slave could not reach these nodes */
    }
}

int command_start(uint8_t slave, uint16_t speed)
{
    uint8_t data[3];

    data[0] = (uint8_t) (speed & 0xFFU);
    data[1] = (uint8_t) (speed >> 8);
    data[2] = 1U; /* mode */
    return baton_node_send(&node, slave, BATON_MSG_CMD_START, data, 3U, BATON_PRIO_HIGH);
}

Set config.role = BATON_ROLE_MASTER, own_address = master_address, and on_poll_done. cycle_period_ms spaces the cycles when the bus should not be busy all the time.

docs.title: Events and states
docs.text:
baton_node_send() (event) baton_node_publish() (state) Destination One node or BATON_ADDR_BROADCAST Every other node Storage Copied into the HIGH or NORMAL queue Overwrites the mailbox Can fail for lack of space Yes: BATON_ERR_FULL Never Delivery Exactly once, in order per source, destination and priority The latest value; intermediate ones may be skipped Undeliverable Dropped after event_ttl_ms, on_drop Sent again until acknowledged

When baton_node_send() returns BATON_ERR_FULL, keep the event and try again later, or drop it deliberately — the library never drops silently.

docs.title: Return values
docs.text: Code Value Returned when BATON_OK 0 Success BATON_ERR_PARAM −1 NULL data with a non-zero length, invalid configuration BATON_ERR_NOT_INIT −2 The node is NULL or not initialized BATON_ERR_MSG_ID −3 Unknown id, or a state id passed to send / an event id to publish BATON_ERR_LEN −4 Length above the MAX_LEN of the message BATON_ERR_ADDR −5 Unknown destination, or the node itself BATON_ERR_FULL −6 The event queue has no room

docs.title: Diagnostics
docs.text:
baton_node_get_stats() copies the counters (see Error handling):

void print_link_health(void)
{
    struct baton_stats stats;

    baton_node_get_stats(&node, &stats);
    log_value("crc_errors", stats.crc_errors);     /* noise on the line */
    log_value("ack_timeouts", stats.ack_timeouts); /* a peer does not answer */
    log_value("queue_used", stats.queue_normal_used);
}

Rising crc_errors and rx_timeouts point to the physical layer; collisions should stay 0 — a non-zero value means two nodes transmitted at once (wrong topology on one node, two masters, or a node with another slave list).

docs.title: The codec without the node
docs.text:
The codec works on its own, for example in a bus monitor that prints every frame:

static struct baton_parser monitor;

void monitor_byte(uint8_t byte)
{
    if (baton_parser_feed(&monitor, byte) == 1)
    {
        const struct baton_frame* f = &monitor.frame;

        print_frame(f->src, f->dst, baton_ctrl_type(f->ctrl), baton_ctrl_seq(f->ctrl),
                    f->payload, f->length);
    }
}

Call baton_parser_init(&monitor) once before the first byte.

docs.title: Common mistakes
docs.text: Symptom Cause baton_node_init() returns BATON_ERR_PARAM A field of the configuration, see Set up a node; often slot_time_ms too short for the baud rate and payload The master polls, slaves never answer Different slave_addresses order or master_address on some node; the slave UART does not receive (wiring, idle level) tx_timeouts grows The write function does not start the UART, or rx_echo is true on a transceiver without echo collisions grows Two masters, or a node with another topology; on RS-485 the transceiver is switched to receive too late bad_messages grows The nodes are built with different message lists rx_overflows grows baton_node_process() is called too rarely for BATON_RX_BUF_SIZE Events dropped (on_drop) Destination offline, or event_ttl_ms shorter than a few cycles BATON_ERR_FULL Queues too small for the traffic during event_ttl_ms, or a destination offline

The application provides baton_user_config.h on the include path (copy config/baton_user_config_template.h). docs.title: Detailed Description
docs.text:
The link owns the receive ring (filled from the UART interrupt), a parser with an inter-byte timeout and a transmitter that waits for a silent bus, checks the echo of its own bytes on a single-wire UART and detects a missing end of transmission. It reports what happened as events; the node layer (Node) uses it, applications normally do not call it directly.

The library never reads a clock: every function that needs the time takes now_ms, a monotonic millisecond counter that may wrap.

** **

  • Lifecycle: baton_link_init.
  • Interrupt entry points: baton_link_rx_isr, baton_link_tx_done_isr.
  • Processing: baton_link_receive, baton_link_transmit, baton_link_send, baton_link_cancel.
  • Queries: baton_link_frame, baton_link_rx_busy, baton_link_frame_ms.

docs.title: Detailed Description
docs.text:
The master passes the baton (POLL) to the slaves in a fixed order; only the polled slave transmits, for at most slot_time_ms, so the bus never has collisions. Messages are of two classes, defined by the application message lists in baton_user_config.h: * EVENT: queued (HIGH or NORMAL priority), acknowledged, retransmitted, delivered exactly once and in order per (source, destination, priority), dropped after event_ttl_ms with an on_drop report; * STATE: a mailbox per state; the latest value is delivered to every other node, intermediate values may be skipped, it can never overflow.

Threading model: baton_node_init(), baton_node_process() and baton_node_get_stats() run in one context (main loop or one RTOS task). baton_node_rx_isr() and baton_node_tx_done_isr() are called from the UART interrupts. baton_node_send() and baton_node_publish() may be called from any context only when enter_critical and exit_critical are configured.

All memory is inside struct baton_node, owned by the caller. No function blocks, allocates memory or reads a clock.

** **

  • Lifecycle: baton_node_default_config, baton_node_init.
  • Processing: baton_node_process.
  • Messages: baton_node_send, baton_node_publish.
  • Interrupt entry points: baton_node_rx_isr, baton_node_tx_done_isr.
  • Diagnostics: baton_node_get_stats.

docs.title: function baton_parser_feed
docs.text:
Feed one byte to the incremental frame parser. 

int baton_parser_feed (
    struct baton_parser * parser,
    uint8_t byte
)

The parser waits for SYNC, reads the header, rejects a LEN above BATON_MAX_PAYLOAD as soon as it is read, then reads the payload and the CRC and validates it. After a valid or invalid frame it waits for the next SYNC. Bytes of a rejected frame are not re-scanned for SYNC; the inter-byte timeout of the link resynchronizes a broken stream.

Parameters:

  • parser Parser state.
  • byte Next byte from the input stream.

Return value:

  • 1 A complete valid frame is available in parser->frame until the next call.
  • 0 More bytes are required.
  • BATON_PARSE_ERROR NULL parser, LEN out of range, CRC mismatch or corrupted state.

docs.title: Detailed Description
docs.text:
Layout rules: * A record is a 16-byte header (baton_record, serialized byte by byte) followed by the data, padded to a multiple of 4 bytes. * A record is never split at the end of the buffer. If it does not fit at the end, a SKIP marker is written there (when a header fits) and the record goes to offset 0. A reader that reaches an offset without room for a header, or a SKIP marker, continues at 0. * head == tail means empty; the producer resets both to 0 when the queue is empty, so the wrapped state never starts from a stale head. * Records are released only from the head.

The producer (baton_node_send()) may run in an interrupt; it calls baton_queue_alloc with the critical section held and publishes a record by setting BATON_REC_VALID last.

#ifndef BATON_DEFS_H
#define BATON_DEFS_H

#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stdint.h>

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C"
{
#endif

#define BATON_SYNC 0xA5U
#define BATON_HEADER_SIZE 5U
#define BATON_CRC_SIZE 2U
#define BATON_FRAME_OVERHEAD (BATON_HEADER_SIZE + BATON_CRC_SIZE)
#define BATON_ADDR_BROADCAST 0xFFU

#define BATON_FT_POLL 0U
#define BATON_FT_RESP 1U
#define BATON_FT_DATA 2U
#define BATON_FT_ACK 3U

#define BATON_ACKB_VALID 0x80U
#define BATON_SEQ_MASK 0x0FU
#define BATON_TLV_HEADER_SIZE 2U

static inline uint8_t baton_ctrl(uint8_t type, bool first, uint8_t seq)
{
    const uint8_t first_bit = first ? 0x20U : 0x00U;

    return (uint8_t) ((uint8_t) ((uint8_t) (type & 0x03U) << 6U) | first_bit
                      | (uint8_t) (seq & BATON_SEQ_MASK));
}

static inline uint8_t baton_ctrl_type(uint8_t ctrl)
{
    return (uint8_t) (ctrl >> 6U);
}

static inline bool baton_ctrl_first(uint8_t ctrl)
{
    return (ctrl & 0x20U) != 0U;
}

static inline uint8_t baton_ctrl_seq(uint8_t ctrl)
{
    return (uint8_t) (ctrl & BATON_SEQ_MASK);
}

static inline uint16_t baton_get_u16be(const uint8_t* data)
{
    return (uint16_t) ((uint16_t) ((uint16_t) data[0] << 8U) | (uint16_t) data[1]);
}

static inline void baton_put_u16be(uint8_t* data, uint16_t value)
{
    data[0] = (uint8_t) (value >> 8U);
    data[1] = (uint8_t) (value & 0xFFU);
}

static inline uint32_t baton_get_u32le(const uint8_t* data)
{
    return (uint32_t) data[0] | ((uint32_t) data[1] << 8U) | ((uint32_t) data[2] << 16U)
           | ((uint32_t) data[3] << 24U);
}

static inline void baton_put_u32le(uint8_t* data, uint32_t value)
{
    data[0] = (uint8_t) (value & 0xFFU);
    data[1] = (uint8_t) ((value >> 8U) & 0xFFU);
    data[2] = (uint8_t) ((value >> 16U) & 0xFFU);
    data[3] = (uint8_t) (value >> 24U);
}

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif

#endif /* BATON_DEFS_H */

/* ==============================================================================
